stories.title: Imran's key message from jail is to 'stick firmly to the ideology': PTI secretary general
summary: Incarcerated PTI founder Imran Khan wants his party leaders to “stick firmly to the ideology” of the party, PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja said on Thursday.
Regarding directives issued by Imran on a possible 28th constitutional amendment, the PTI secretary general said he would put this matter before the party leadership first.
He was then asked about the government’s knowledge of the matter, considering the lengthy meeting allowed Imran to discuss political issues with his lawyers.

stories.title: 11 killed, 2 injured as passenger van plunges into river in GB's Ghizer: police
summary: GILGIT: Eleven people were killed and two injured when a passenger vehicle plunged into a river in Gilgit-Baltistan’s Ghizer district on Thursday.
Last week, eight people were killed and 30 others injured when a passenger bus travelling from Gilgit to Islamabad collided with a dumper truck near the Havelian Interchange on the Hazara Motorway.
The day before, a collision between a passenger bus and a truck claimed the lives of 11 people and left 33 others injured near Punjab’s Pakpattan.

On Sept 17, the government rolled out the Prime Minister’s Fuel Relief Scheme across the country to ease the public’s burden amid rising fuel prices due to the Middle East situation.

stories.title: One dead, four wounded in downtown Washington shooting: police chief
summary: One person was killed and four were wounded in a shooting at and outside a fitness center in an upscale residential neighborhood of downtown Washington on Thursday, police said.

Jeffery Carroll, Washington’s interim police chief, told reporters the suspect in the shooting had been found with a self-inflicted gunshot wound after barricading himself in his nearby apartment unit.
Multiple law enforcement agencies could be seen at the scene of the shooting and police helicopters were hovering over the area.

stories.title: Sindh govt to launch crackdown on encroachments on Karachi's main thoroughfares, including University Road
summary: According to the statement, the concerned departments were directed to take “immediate measures” to remove established encroachments along the bus service routes as well as illegal encroachments that blocked traffic flow.
It was also decided that measures would be taken to shift illegal bus terminals established in various parts of the city, including Sohrab Goth, to outside the city.

Memon directed the concerned officials to accelerate efforts for the establishment of a logistics park, saying that “all relevant departments should work together to improve traffic flow in the city and organise the transport system”, the statement concluded.

stories.title: Sukuk stock crosses Rs10tr
summary: The discussion also covered the direction and targets for expanding digital payments, in light of progress under the prime minister's initiative.

Raast payment QR codes have been placed on more than 45 million gas and electricity bills, all National Database and Registration Authority centres have been equipped to accept them, and the overall volume of digital payments has doubled in a year.

He will meet the presidents and chief executives of banks in Karachi to discuss the initiative and the promotion of digital payments, so that all banks can play their part in this national initiative.

stories.title: PSX retreats again from 180,000 mark
summary: At the close of trading, the KSE-100 index fell 1,710.04 points, or 0.95%, and settled at 177,373.76.
Topline's market review stated that the PSX witnessed a bearish trading session on Thursday, as selling pressure weighed on investor sentiment.
The benchmark KSE-100 index declined 1,710 points (-0.95%) to close at 177,374, reflecting cautious investor positioning and profit-taking across the market.

stories.title: Nvidia crisis wipes $1tr off market value
summary: Global AI-linked stocks were trading lower after bouncing off their sessions lows on Thursday, as investors weighed the fallout of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure on the sector, which is already pressured by funding and regulatory concerns.

Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will take over as interim CEO as Nvidia looks for a permanent successor, the company said, after news of Huang's two extramarital affairs plunged the chipmaker into its worst crisis ever.
The biggest hammering came on Sunday after Nvidia's board announced an investigation into Huang's relationship with a businesswoman called Alice Huang, who is alleged to be a Chinese spy.

stories.title: Hormuz disruptions lift oil prices
summary: Oil prices rose on Thursday by more than $1 a barrel, as continued disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and broader geopolitical tensions offset pressure from rising crude output that had sent prices lower in early trade.
In the strait, tankers are still ablaze, oil spills are washing ashore, and drones and missiles have hit infrastructure across the region.
On Thursday, Iran's military said four oil tankers were hit by explosions in the Strait of Hormuz after ignoring warnings.

stories.title: Safe AI use in everyday lives urged
summary: A recent survey conducted by Kaspersky in the META region shows that AI is becoming part of consumers' everyday lives and users are increasingly turning to AI services for personal matters, raising new privacy and cybersecurity concerns.
Almost 79% of respondents across the Middle East, Turkiye and Africa (META) region reported using AI services, including smart chatbots and image and video generation tools.

The most common use of AI is searching for and summarising information, reported by 74% of respondents, followed by writing texts at 50%, generating images from text descriptions or prompts at 42%, editing or transforming personal photos at 41%, and creating videos at 32%.

stories.title: PTA halts internet service to unlicensed entities
summary: The meeting highlighted the District Class Licence, enabling Pemra cable operators and last-mile service providers to obtain bandwidth from FLL licensees.

It was reiterated that LDI and FLL licensees may provide bandwidth, including configured packages, exclusively to PTA-licensed operators and are prohibited from supplying IP bandwidth, panel services, E1s, DPLCs or similar services to unlicensed entities or distributors.
"Internet service bills/receipts must be issued by the relevant FLL or Class Licensee, as applicable," it said.

stories.title: Jensen Huang steps down as Nvidia CEO after reports of extramarital affairs
summary: Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive of Nvidia on Thursday, ending his 33-year run at the helm of the AI giant he co-founded after revelations that he had two extramarital affairs, including with a woman accused of spying for China.

Nvidia’s board met on Wednesday to consider his ouster, a person familiar with the matter said, after reports earlier in the day that Huang also had an extramarital affair with a senior company executive who reported to him.
Trump said on Sunday that Huang had “done an amazing job for our country” and that the Nvidia chief had told him he had no idea the Chinese woman he had an affair with was a spy.

stories.title: CEC Raja alleges federal govt wants to 'sabotage' Islamabad local govt polls
summary: ISLAMABAD: Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Sikandar Sultan Raja on Thursday accused the federal government of trying to sabotage the local government elections in Islamabad, clarifying that the polls would be held as scheduled.

During the hearing, ECP Secretary Omar Hamid recalled that a candidate of the Pakistan Markazi Muslim League (PMML) had filed an application with the district returning officer, stating that Information Minister Attaullah Tarar and Farooq Tarar had visited NA-77.
The PkMAP chief’s name has also been removed, as the case of its intra-party elections and an amendment to its constitution remains pending before the ECP.

stories.title: Naqvi suggests referendum as 'solution' to debate on new administrative units
summary: Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Thursday suggested that political parties hold a referendum to gauge the public’s opinion on the creation of new administrative units or provinces, terming it the “solution” to the ongoing debate.

[But], if the public says they should be made, then they should.” Naqvi noted that political parties had varying stances on the debate, with the PPP “having its own stance [and] some parties having their own stance while not saying anything officially”.

Naqvi claims he and Bilawal ‘nearly on same page’ Responding to another question, Naqvi recalled recent remarks by PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari, wherein he had called for a “political reset” and encouraged unity among political parties.

stories.title: Power shutdown at Dhabeji to cause Karachi-wide water shortage tomorrow
summary: According to a KWSC spokesperson, KE has formally notified the water utility of the scheduled power shutdown. “Electricity supply to Dhabeji Grid Station will remain suspended on Nov 13 for annual maintenance,” he said.
During this period, only three pumps at Dhabeji would remain non-operational, resulting in a partial disruption of water supply to Landhi, Korangi, Malir and Shah Faisal.
Meanwhile, a KE spokesperson said the scheduled maintenance shutdown at Dhabeji Grid Station would take place on Friday and that advance notice had been shared with the KWSC.

stories.title: Nepra notifies Rs25.30 per unit revised special industrial tariff despite concerns
summary: ISLAMABAD: The National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (Nepra) on Thursday notified a Rs25.30 per unit revised incremental consumption package (ICP) for industry and agriculture to encourage higher consumption.

Industrial consumers complained that the Rs25.30 per unit revised ICP — against the actual marginal cost of Rs31.83 or Rs29.65 per unit calculated by Nepra —resulted in higher monthly fuel cost adjustments (FCAs) and burdened all consumer categories across the country.

Nepra chairman Mukhtar fully endorsed the written arguments and positions taken by the dissenting members, but subsequently exercised his special casting vote to approve the revised rate of Rs25.30 per unit.

stories.title: Three terrorists killed as security forces foil attack on N-25 in Mastung: state media
summary: Security forces killed three terrorists on National Highway N-25 in Balochistan's Mastung district on Thursday, Radio Pakistan reported on Thursday, citing police.

Read: Soldier martyred, 17 terrorists killed in Balochistan IBOs: ISPR The police statement said that the security forces repulsed the attack through "timely and effective action", noting that in the ensuing retaliatory operation, three terrorists were killed.
On November 3, a soldier was martyred while security forces killed 17 militants in two intelligence-based operations in Balochistan’s Kachhi and Kharan districts.

stories.title: Setback for Google as EU Court adviser backs $1.7b antitrust fine
summary: Google suffered a setback on Thursday ‌as an adviser to Europe's top court faulted a lower tribunal's decision to scrap a €1.49 billion ($1.7 billion) fine levied against the US ​tech giant seven years ago for anti-competitive practices related ​to online advertising.
The General Court rejected the EU decision in ⁠2024, prompting the Commission to appeal to the Luxembourg-based ​Court of Justice of the European Union.
Google, ‌whose ⁠AdSense platform provides search advertising, removed the contested clauses from publisher agreements in 2016.

stories.title: Raja says Imran urges PTI leaders to stand firm on ideology, rejects compromise for political gains
summary: Speaking to a local television programme, Capital Talk, Raja said Imran had conveyed his message to party leaders through Safdar, urging them to stand firm on the party’s ideology.
Quoting Imran, Raja said the PTI founder had described Allama Nasir and Pakhtunkhwa Milli Awami Party (PkMAP) chief Mahmood Khan Achakzai as people who would neither bow down nor be bought.

Asked whether Safdar’s delivery of a political message could lead to restrictions on future meetings with the PTI founder, Raja said the conversation involving Safdar and senior lawyer Latif Khosa had not been held secretly. “The discussion was not concealed.

stories.title: India probes website blocks based on forged court orders
summary: India has launched an inquiry into how telecoms officials blocked websites based on forged court orders, while police have sought ministry records as part of a criminal investigation, officials said on Thursday.

Police opened a criminal investigation after checks by the Allahabad High Court found that one of the purported orders in its name cited by the ministry had not been issued by the court, according to police documents reviewed by Reuters.

Ghanshyam Yadav, a cybercrime official in Uttar Pradesh, said police had asked the telecoms ministry for details of its content management system and digital logs to understand how it processed the forged orders and help identify those responsible.

stories.title: OpenAI, Google, Anthropic hit with lawsuit seeking halt to frontier AI development
summary: Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier sued OpenAI in June, accusing the company of misrepresenting the safety of its ChatGPT platform, saying it has harmed children by providing information to school shooters, offering guidance on self-harm and addicting young users.
Separately, a group of eight states sued OpenAI last month in courts across the country alleging ChatGPT ⁠has coached ​its users — including teenagers — to harm themselves or others.
The states' lawsuits seek financial penalties, as well as an order barring the company from developing self-improving AI models unless it ​can ensure those models are aligned with human values.

stories.title: A possible Xi-Trump-Putin summit evokes 1945 Yalta carve-up of world
summary: A possible China-US-Russia summit has prompted alarm of a modern-day Yalta Conference, with three powerful men carving up the world — with little regard for Ukraine, Europe and Taiwan or anyone else.
That meeting in Yalta, then in the Soviet Union and now in a part of Ukraine annexed by Russia in 2014, laid out the foundations for the Soviet domination of Eastern Europe and the Cold War.

China has opposed the logic of Yalta — the clandestine division of spheres of influence and major powers determining the fate of other nations — “from the very beginning”, according to Renmin University’s Wang.

stories.title: Canadian mining company signs MoU with Mari Energies in South Asia push
summary: Mari Energies’ mining unit, Mari Minerals, has multiple mineral exploration projects, including copper and gold in Pakistan.
He said Pakistan possessed substantial and diverse mineral resources, including significant copper and gold potential along the Tethyan metallogenic belt in the west of the country.

The Reko Diq copper-gold project in Balochistan is one of Pakistan’s most ambitious mining ventures, with significant potential to boost the country’s mineral wealth through the extraction of gold and copper.

stories.title: Rana Sanaullah refutes 'conspiracy theories' linking relaxation meted out to Imran with 'discussion' on proposed 28th Amendment
summary: Lawyers representing the PTI met Imran on November 11, a day after the Islamabad High Court (IHC) ordered authorities to facilitate the meeting.
Despite this, access to Imran and Bushra Bibi at Adiala Jail has remained restricted, with meetings between the PTI founder and his lawyers becoming increasingly infrequent.
However, Safdar was not allowed to meet both his clients again until November 2, when jail authorities facilitated a 40-minute meeting with Imran and Bushra.

stories.title: At COP31, PM Shehbaz calls for grant-based finance, resilience funding for climate-vulnerable countries
summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday called for grant-based finance and improved resilience and adaptation funds for climate-vulnerable countries at COP31, being held in Turkiye’s Antalya.

It said PM Shehbaz reaffirmed Pakistan’s desire to “translate the longstanding and friendly relations into a forward-looking partnership encompassing trade and investment, education and skills development, technology, climate resilience and people-to-people contacts”.
The prime minister also held several bilateral conversations with world leaders and international organisations on the sidelines of the summit on Wednesday.

stories.title: PTI lawmaker moves FCC seeking immediate release of Sohail Afridi, other party workers
summary: ISLAMABAD: PTI lawmaker Shandana Gulzar on Thursday approached the Federal Constitutional Court (FCC), seeking the immediate release of Sohail Afridi, the non-functional Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chief minister, the provincial assembly speaker and other party workers.

In her petition, Gulzar requested the FCC to order the immediate release of the detained PTI leaders subject to any lawful order passed by a competent court in accordance with the Constitution and the law.

The petition has also pleaded before FCC to modify its Nov 5 order to the extent that the petitions challenging governor’s rule and state of emergency in KP before the high court should not remain suspended.

stories.title: Board of Peace urges 'immediate' implementation of Trump’s Gaza plan after Israeli hospital strike
summary: The Board of Peace said on Thursday that US President Donald Trump's Gaza peace plan must be implemented "immediately without further delay" after a deadly Israeli strike on Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis, in the southern Gaza Strip, while not criticising Israel.

"The special coordinator ad interim is deeply alarmed by the Israeli airstrike on Nasser Hospital in Gaza last night, which killed six people, injured 27 others, and caused extensive damage to the facility," said deputy spokesman Farhan Haq.
Since October 2023, Israel’s war on Gaza has killed more than 74,600 Palestinians and wounded nearly 176,000.

stories.title: Naqvi makes surprise dash to Nawabshah with ‘important message’ for Zardari
summary: Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi made an unscheduled visit to Nawabshah on Thursday night and held a nearly hour-long meeting with President Asif Ali Zardari at Zardari House, amid speculation over discussions on key political developments.

The meeting came hours after Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said he and Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari were largely on the same page regarding a reset of the system, referring to the latter’s remarks a day earlier.
On the question of creating new provinces, Naqvi urged political parties to seek public opinion through a referendum.

stories.title: Petrol goes down by Rs3, high-speed diesel by Rs4 for Nov 13
summary: On November 2, the government announced that oil refineries would bear a burden of Rs15 billion per month, which would allow petrol to be sold Rs15 cheaper than it was in the global market amid the US-Israeli war on Iran.
Around 10 million two-wheeler users and 800,000 three-wheeler users would be entitled to relief on 20 litres of fuel per month, translating into a maximum monthly benefit of Rs2,000 per beneficiary.
Another one million users of cars up to 800cc would receive relief on 30 litres per month, providing them with a maximum benefit of Rs3,000 each.

stories.title: Visa barriers push students from US and UK to Asia and Europe, global survey shows
summary: International students are turning away from the United States and Britain in favour of universities in Asia and continental Europe, a global university survey showed ​on Thursday, as tighter visa rules redraw the global map of higher ‌education.

Meanwhile, Britain has tightened its student visa rules as successive ​governments seek to ⁠reduce immigration, restricting most international students from bringing dependants and planning to shorten the period graduates can remain in the country to work or seek employment.

"These survey results affirm what we've observed ⁠before: ​national policies matter to international students making major decisions about ​where to study, conduct research, or start a career," Dr Fanta Aw, the executive director and CEO of NAFSA, ​said.

stories.title: Pakistan-Sri Lanka Test hit by bad weather after Saqib Khan's heroics
summary: Rain and bad light hit the first Test between Pakistan and Sri Lanka after pacer Saqib Khan took seven wickets on debut to lead the home team’s fightback on Thursday.
Kusal, who added 249 runs for the fifth wicket with De Silva, fell to Saqib for 119 in the fifth over after adding just two to his overnight score.
Sri Lanka lost their last six wickets for 42 runs and Saqib took his fifth when Sonal Dinusha (20) edged to slip.

stories.title: UAE says 14 killed, 30 injured in Fujairah traffic accident
summary: At least 14 people were killed and 30 others injured in a pileup involving 18 vehicles and five trucks in Fujairah, an emirate in the United Arab Emirates (UAE), the UAE Ministry of Interior said Thursday.
The ministry added in a post ​on ​X ⁠that emergency and ​specialised teams ​were ⁠continuing to deal with the ⁠aftermath ​of ​the accident.

Ministry of Interior: Authorities Continue Efforts to Address Fujairah Traffic Accident The Ministry of Interior has reported a major multi-vehicle crash in the Emirate of Fujairah involving 18 cars and trucks.

stories.title: Imran’s sisters Uzma, Noreen released from jail after extended detention orders withdrawn, says lawyer
summary: LAHORE: Dr Uzma Khan and Noreen Niazi, sisters of incarcerated PTI founder Imran Khan, were released from Kot Lakhpat jail following the withdrawal of their extended detention orders, PTI legal counsel Rana Mudassar Umer told Dawn on Thursday.

PTI lawyer Taimur Malik also said on X that the two women had been released upon the withdrawal of the “unlawful MPO detention order”. “Everyone else detained under these MPO orders should be released as well,” he said.

Their jailing was arbitrary and so is their release.” Imran’s three sisters — Noreen, Aleema and Uzma — have been in jail on the Lahore deputy commissioner’s (DC) orders as the PTI geared up for a protest march towards Islamabad.

stories.title: China's Xi says Taiwan 'reunification' must happen as history cannot be stopped
summary: Beijing calls Sun a great national hero and patriot, as well as the forerunner of the 1949 communist ​revolution that forced the defeated Republic of ​China government to flee to Taiwan, ⁠where it remains to this day.

While Taiwan President Lai Ching-te and his ruling Democratic Progressive Party champion Taiwan’s separate identity from China, they have been striking a tougher tone with Beijing on the role of the Republic of China.

Taiwan has ⁠been particularly upset ​by Beijing’s effort to claim credit for the victory in World War Two, saying it was the ​Republic of China government that fought alongside the allies, as the People’s Republic of China did not exist at the time.

stories.title: Netflix faces backlash for keeping Russell Brand’s comedy special after conviction
summary: Netflix is facing criticism for keeping Russell Brand’s stand-up special, Russell Brand: Re, in its catalogue following the comedian’s conviction for rape and sexual assault.
Netflix classifies the special as TV-MA.
Others questioned whether Brand continues to receive payments from the special, while some criticised Netflix’s decision to keep it available.

stories.title: Poisonous substance detected in sample after 5 children die in Khyber
summary: Laboratory tests confirmed the presence of a poisonous substance in a sample taken from one of five children who died after a suspected poisoning incident in the Bazaar Zakha Khel area of Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa's Khyber district, officials said on Thursday.
At least seven children were affected by the suspected poisonous substance, five of whom died while two others fell unconscious.
Reports received from Khyber Medical College confirmed the presence of poisonous material in a sample taken from one of the children.

stories.title: ECP strikes MQM-P's Khalid Maqbool off party leadership list
summary: The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) has removed Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui’s name as the convener of Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P) from its official website, leaving the party among 13 political parties without a recognised head in the commission's records.
Meanwhile, the ECP has issued a show-cause notice to MQM-P over its failure to hold intra-party elections.

The removal of Siddiqui's name from the ECP website comes amid the party’s failure to hold fresh intra-party elections within the prescribed timeframe, raising questions about its leadership status in the commission's official records.

stories.title: Fact check: Viral visuals do not show violence in Balochistan; they are unrelated and old
summary: How it started On Nov 10, a pro-PTI account, based on its past posts, shared a video on X allegedly showing a mosque in Balochistan, destroyed with bullet holes and heavy firearms.

A pro-Afghan account later shared the same video with the following caption: “Armed men set several fully loaded trucks on fire near Turbat.” The video was also shared by other smaller accounts here, here, here and here.

A reverse image search was conducted to trace the source of the viral video and yielded a clip shared on Facebook on September 21, 2026, by a Nigerian with the following caption: “This is Malam Fatori.

stories.title: Russell Brand’s Instagram and Facebook accounts disabled by Meta after sentencing
summary: Russell Brand’s social media accounts on platforms owned by Meta have been disabled following his conviction for rape and sexual assault.
Meta, which owns Instagram and Facebook, has disabled Brand’s accounts.
Meta’s community standards policy states that, “in order to maintain a safe environment and empower free expression”, the company restricts or removes accounts considered “harmful to the community”.

stories.title: Two policemen, including ASI, martyred in attack on patrolling party in Swabi: DPO
summary: SWABI: Two policemen, including an assistant sub-inspector (ASI) heading the Mansori police post, were martyred when three suspects opened fire on a patrolling party on Wednesday night, District Police Officer Waqas Rafiq told the media.
The nearby police station was subsequently informed, and personnel reached the scene, where they found Head Constable Shahid Khan, 28, injured.

In his statement to the police, Shahid said that when the patrolling party reached India Cham in the Gohati area, ASI Walid was sitting in the front seat of the vehicle, while he and other policemen were seated in the back.
